associations.rationale: The formal type directly states that every two irreducible-representation vertices are joined by a path whose consecutive McKay multiplicities are positive, which is the requested connectedness of the McKay graph.

The theorem shows that the irreducible dimensions form a null vector of the McKay Cartan matrix, a key characterization used to identify affine-Dynkin marks, but it does not itself state equality with the displayed vertex labels.
For a nontrivial finite subgroup and a complete list of irreducibles, the formal conclusion directly says that the McKay adjacency matrix is an affine Dynkin diagram, matching part (c).
The formal equality of the McKay multiplicities with their transposes directly states the symmetry r_ij = r_ji requested in part (a).
